name: SikaHyflex-305 AP
paste:
SIKAHYFLEX®-305 AP: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaHyflex®-305 AP, November 2023, Version 03.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/v/sikahyflex_-305_ap.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaHyflex®-305 AP where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 03.03).
1.2 Product description. SikaHyflex®-305 AP is a 1-component, moisture curing, low-modulus elastic weather sealant.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaHyflex®-305 AP is designed for weather proofing and sealing applications where durability under severe conditions is required. SikaHyflex®-305 AP is particularly suited for use as a weather sealant for curtain wall and metal cladding facades.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaHyflex®-305 AP
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Weather sealant for curtain wall and metal cladding facades
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - ASTM C 920, class 50
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ASTM C 719: cited elsewhere in the data sheet; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Features (p.1); Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - ASTM C 920: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - ISO 1183-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.1).
    - ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.2).
    - ISO 8339: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Secant tensile modulus (p.2).
    - ISO 9047: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - ISO 7389: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Elastic recovery (p.2).
    - ISO 7390: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Sag flow (p.2).
    - CQP 049-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Curing rate (p.2).
    - CQP 019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Skinning time (p.2); Application Information > Tack free time (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Very good resistance to weathering
    - Movement capability of ±50 % (ASTM C 719)
    - Very good workability
    - Good adhesion to a wide range of substrates
    - Solvent-free
    - Neutral cure
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Neutral cure silicone
    - Colour: Black, Grey
    - Density: ~ 1.50 kg/l (ISO 1183-1)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: ~ 25 (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Secant tensile modulus: ~ 0.35 N/mm² at 100% elongation (23 °C ); ~ 0.40 N/mm² at 100% elongation (−20°C) (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~ 800% (ISO 37)
    - Movement capability: ± 25%; ± 50% (ISO 9047) (ASTM C 719)
    - Elastic recovery: ~ 80% (ISO 7389)
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~ 4.5 N/mm (ISO 34)
    - Service temperature: −40 °C to +150 °C
    - Resistance to weathering: 10 (ISO / DIS 19862)
2.7 Joint design. The joint width must be designed to suit the joint movement required and the movement capability of the sealant. The joint width shall be ≥ 6 mm and ≤ 45 mm. The joint depth shall be ≥ 6 mm and ≤ 15 mm. A width to depth ratio of 2:1 must be maintained (for exceptions, see table below). Typical joint dimensions
    | Joint Width [mm] | Joint Depth [mm] |
    | 10 | 6 |
    | 15 | 8 |
    | 20 | 10 |
    | 30 | 15 |
    | 45 | 15 |
    All joints must be correctly designed and dimensioned in accordance with the relevant standards, before their construction. The basis for calculation of the necessary joint widths are the type of structure and its dimensions, the technical values of the adjacent building materials and the joint sealing material, as well as the specific exposure of the building and the joints. For larger joints please contact Sika technical service.
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 600 ml foil pack, 20 foil packs per box
    - Storage conditions: SikaHyflex®-305 AP shall be stored in dry conditions, where it is protected from direct sunlight and at temperatures between +5 °C and +25 °C.
2.9 Shelf life. SikaHyflex®-305 AP has a shelf life of 12 months for cartridges and 15 months for foil packs from the date of production, if it is stored in undamaged, original, sealed packaging, and if the storage conditions are met.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 03.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be clean, dry, sound and homogeneous, free from oils, grease, dust and loose or friable particles. The following priming and/or pre-treatment procedures shall be followed:
    - Non-porous substrates
    - Float glass, coated glass, anodised aluminium and stainless steel have to be pre-treated using Sika® Aktivator-205, Sika® Aktivator-100 or Sika® Cleaner P. Powder coated and PVDF coated metals have to be pre-treated using Sika® Aktivator-205. For details like application and flash-off times refer to the most recent PDS of the respective pre-treatment product.
    - Porous substrates
    - Concrete, aerated concrete and cement based renders, mortars and bricks shall be primed using Sika® Primer-3 N or Sika® Primer-210. For details like application and flash-off times refer to the most recent PDS of the respective pre-treatment product. Adhesion tests on project specific substrates must be performed prior to application. For more detailed advice and instructions please contact Sika technical service. Note: Primers are adhesion promoters. They are neither a substitute for the correct cleaning of a surface, nor do they improve the strength of the surface significantly.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 03.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Sag flow: ~ 2 mm (20 mm profile, 50 °C) (ISO 7390)
    - Backing material: Use closed cell, polyethylene foam backing rods.
    - Curing rate: ~ 2 mm/24 hours (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~ 25 minutes (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
    - Tack free time: ~ 160 minutes (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
4.3 Compatibility. SikaHyflex®-305 AP is compatible with most SikaHyflex® and Sikasil® silicone weather sealants, Sikasil® SG adhesives and Sikasil® IG sealants. All other sealants and adhesives have to be approved by Sika before using them in direct contact with SikaHyflex®-305 AP. Where two or more different reactive sealants and/or adhesives are used, allow the first one to cure completely before applying the next one. For specific information regarding compatibility contact Sika technical service.
4.4 Consumption.
    | Joint length [m] | Joint width [mm] | Joint depth [mm] |
    | per 600 ml foil pack |
    | 10 | 10 | 6 |
    | 5 | 15 | 8 |
    | 3 | 20 | 10 |
    | 2 | 25 | 12 |
    | 1.3 | 30 | 15 |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.5 Application method / tools.
    - SikaHyflex®-305 AP is supplied ready to use.
    - After the necessary substrate preparation, insert a suitable backing rod to the required depth and apply pre-treatment if necessary. Insert a foil pack or cartridge into the sealant gun and extrude SikaHyflex®-305 AP into the joint making sure that it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoids any air entrapment. SikaHyflex®-305 AP sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion.
    - It is recommended to use masking tape where exact joint lines or neat lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time.
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use with Sika® Remover-208 and/or Sika® TopClean T. Once cured, residual material can only be removed mechanically.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - SikaHyflex®-305 AP cannot be overpainted.
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals or other extreme external influences. However, a change in colour is purely of aesthetic nature and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - Do not use SikaHyflex®-305 AP on natural stone.
    - Do not use SikaHyflex®-305 AP on bituminous substrates, natural rubber or any building materials which might bleed oils, plasticizers or solvents that could attack the sealant. EPDM or other gaskets in direct contact with SikaHyflex®-305 AP have to be tested for compatibility prior to application. For specific advice contact Sika technical service.
    - Do not use SikaHyflex®-305 AP on pre-stressed polyacrylate and polycarbonate as it may cause environmental stress cracking (crazing).
    - Do not use SikaHyflex®-305 AP to seal joints in and around swimming pools.
    - Do not use SikaHyflex®-305 AP for joints under water pressure or for permanent water immersion.
    - Do not expose uncured SikaHyflex®-305 AP to alcohol containing products as this may interfere with the curing reaction.
4.8 Further information.
    - Safety Data Sheet (SDS)
    - Pre-treatment Chart Sealing & Bonding
    - General Guidelines SikaHyflex and Sikasil Weather Sealants

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C to +40 °C, min. 3 °C above dew point temperature
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C to +40 °C
5.4 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: ~ 1.50 kg/l (ISO 1183-1)
    - Shore A hardness: ~ 25 (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Secant tensile modulus: ~ 0.35 N/mm² at 100% elongation (23 °C ); ~ 0.40 N/mm² at 100% elongation (−20°C) (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~ 800% (ISO 37)
    - Movement capability: ± 25%; ± 50% (ISO 9047) (ASTM C 719)
    - Elastic recovery: ~ 80% (ISO 7389)
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~ 4.5 N/mm (ISO 34)
    - Resistance to weathering: 10 (ISO / DIS 19862)
    - Sag flow: ~ 2 mm (20 mm profile, 50 °C) (ISO 7390)
    - Curing rate: ~ 2 mm/24 hours (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~ 25 minutes (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
    - Tack free time: ~ 160 minutes (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaHyflex®-305 AP, November 2023, Version 03.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/v/sikahyflex_-305_ap.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaHyflex®-305 AP, version 20/01/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/sds-sikahyflex-305ap.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
